source.author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
source.work: Letters from a Stoic & On the Shortness of Life

entries.text: We suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
It is not that we have a short time to live, but that we waste a lot of it.
Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity.
Every new beginning comes from some other beginning's end.
If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
As long as you live, keep learning how to live.
Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
The greatest remedy for anger is delay.
Life is long enough, and has been given in sufficiently generous measure, if you should decide to invest all of it wisely.
You learn to know a pilot in a storm.
Every night before going to sleep, we must ask ourselves: what weakness have I overcome today? What virtue have I acquired?
No great thing is created suddenly.
Religion is regarded by the common people as true, by the wise as false, and by rulers as useful.
He who is brave is free.
Begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
Sometimes even to live is an act of courage.
Those who have been great, lived a life of dignity and purpose. It is not length of life, but depth of life.
The whole future lies in uncertainty: live immediately.
Wherever there is a human being, there is an opportunity for kindness.
A gem cannot be polished without friction, nor a man perfected without trials.
Only time can heal what reason cannot.
All cruelty springs from weakness.
True happiness is to enjoy the present, without anxious dependence upon the future.
Associate with people who are likely to improve you.
The bravest sight in the world is to see a great man struggling against adversity.
